questions.prompt: Sort each element into its family.
questions.explain: Group 1: alkali metals; group 17: halogens; group 18: noble gases.

questions.prompt: Order the alkali metals from LEAST to MOST reactive with water.
Order the halogens from MOST to LEAST reactive.
Why are noble gases so unreactive?
questions.explain: A full outer shell is stable.

questions.prompt: Match each halogen to its appearance at room temperature.
questions.explain: Halogens get darker and change from gas to liquid to solid going down the group.

questions.prompt: What do all alkali metals produce when they react with water?
options: Hydrogen and an alkaline solution (metal hydroxide)

questions.prompt: Why does reactivity INCREASE down group 1?
options: The outer electron is further from the nucleus and is lost more easily
questions.explain: Bigger atoms hold their single outer electron less tightly.

questions.prompt: Match each noble gas to a use.
questions.explain: Their lack of reactivity makes them safe for these uses.

questions.prompt: Predict the properties of astatine (below iodine in group 17) and explain your predictions.
questions.modelAnswer: Astatine will be a dark (black) solid, even darker than iodine, and it will be the least reactive halogen. Going down group 17, halogens get darker, change from gas to liquid to solid, and become less reactive because bigger atoms attract an extra electron less strongly.
rubric: Predicted it is less reactive than iodine
Explained using the trend / atom size
questions.explain: Trends let you predict elements you've never seen.
